subject: Justin Tseng Legislative Priorities
overview: The Medford Bytes podcast interviewed newly elected City Councilor Justin Tseng regarding his goals for school funding, climate action, and language justice. The episode also provided updates on the city's Charter Review process and commemorated Black History Month through the story of Belinda Sutton.

items.title: Belinda Sutton and Black History Month
items.summary: Host Danielle Balocca shared the history of Belinda Sutton, whose 1783 petition for a pension from the Royal family estate is an early narrative of an enslaved woman.

items.title: Charter Review Update
items.summary: Balocca announced that the Mayor is seeking a City Council vote on a home rule petition to elect a Charter Review Commission.

items.title: Motivations for Running
items.summary: Councilor Justin Tseng cited 2020 school budget cuts and the 2020 racial justice movement as his primary motivations for seeking office.

items.title: Inclusivity at City Hall
items.summary: Tseng discussed the importance of changing City Council rules and institutional culture to foster a more inclusive environment for marginalized groups.

items.title: Campaign Reflections
items.summary: Tseng reflected on his campaign, noting that neighborhood priorities varied significantly between concerns like flooding and infrastructure needs.

items.title: Charter Review and Ward Representation
items.summary: Tseng voiced support for the Charter Review process and the potential adoption of ward representation to better serve local neighborhoods.

items.title: First Term Goals
items.summary: Councilor Tseng outlined his term goals, focusing on increased school funding, ambitious climate policies, and improved communication with residents.

items.title: Language Justice and Accessibility
items.summary: Tseng advocated for "language justice" by proposing professional translations for city services and guides to improve accessibility for non-English speakers.
